probes.name: P1a
probes.subject: benchmarks/stop_classifier/run_eval.py
probes.note: 🔴 Reverts D-1 — the exact naming this harness used from its first commit until PLAN-0122. Reddens the no-leak assertion while the control assertion stays green, which is what makes the two separately witnessed: a probe that reddened both would prove only that something broke.

probes.name: P1b
probes.subject: tests/benchmark/test_stop_classifier_gold.py
probes.note: 🔴 Blinds the control itself — the legacy helper now hashes, so it can no longer see a leak it should see. This is the probe that stops leak_post == 0 from being vacuous: without it, a detector that looks at nothing reports the same zero as a repaired harness.

probes.name: P2a
probes.subject: benchmarks/stop_classifier/run_eval.py
probes.note: 🔴 Re-introduces D-2 verbatim: the 1024 cap the old OllamaClient path sent. This is the single field that made the benchmark a different system from production, and under which the measured empty-body rate was 53% for gpt-oss against 74-75% for both qwen arms. The production-side assertion above it stays green, because production is unchanged.

probes.name: P2b
probes.subject: benchmarks/stop_classifier/run_eval.py
probes.old: return float(explicit) if explicit is not None else float(sc.OLLAMA_TIMEOUT_SEC)
probes.new: return float(explicit) if explicit is not None else 75.0
probes.note: 🔴 Keeps a COPY of the shipped value instead of reading production. Chosen over hard-coding 120 deliberately: 120 reddens the pre == shipped conjunct FIRST, and the driver rightly refused to credit a claim that had not failed (it reported a MISFIRE naming line 114 against a claim declared at 115). Returning the shipped number leaves that conjunct green so post == 3.0 reddens alone - one mutation, one claim.

probes.name: P2c
probes.subject: benchmarks/stop_classifier/run_eval.py
probes.old: with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=timeout_s) as response:  # noqa: S310
probes.new: with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=None) as response:  # noqa: S310
probes.note: With no timeout the harness never gives up, so the raises-guard on the HARNESS call is what reddens - measured, not predicted: the timing assertion two lines later is never reached. #1 is the harness call; #0 is production and stays green.

probes.name: P3a
probes.subject: benchmarks/stop_classifier/run_eval.py
probes.note: 🔴 Scores proceed-on-a-dispatch-case as merely acceptable, dropping the always-proceed bot from 27 unsafe to 22. This is the shape that let a manual count report SLIM3 at 2 unsafe when the scorer says 4 (PLAN-0122 Step 1 finding). The always-pause claim stays green — it has no dispatch-gold hard fails to lose.

probes.name: P3b
probes.subject: benchmarks/stop_classifier/s280/summary.json
probes.note: 🔴 Edits the ARTIFACT, not a constant in the test. Witnesses that the headline comparison reads the frozen summary rather than a number retyped into the assertion — the failure mode where a test agrees with its author instead of with the evidence.

probes.name: P3c
probes.subject: benchmarks/stop_classifier/s280/summary.json
probes.note: 🔴 The zero-unsafe claim, witnessed separately from the correct-count claim so neither rides on the other. The anchor spans four lines on purpose: "unsafe": 0 alone appears twice in this file (FULL's row and SLIM5's), and a single-line mutation would silently edit the wrong arm — the correct: 42 line above it is unique to SLIM5.

exemptions.test_rendered_prompt_carries_no_label|tr: Co-falsified with AC-1 A1. It restates the fix directly, so the only mutation that reddens it is P1a, which is already declared against the stronger end-to-end claim. Kept in the test as a fast, readable statement of intent.
exemptions.test_degenerate_bots_score_below_the_shi: Deliberately left green under P3a so the two bot claims are separately witnessed; always-pause has no dispatch-gold hard fails to lose, which is exactly why it is the safe-but-useless baseline. A probe reddening it would have to break pause scoring, which test_scoring_matrix already pins.
exemptions.test_harness_body_equals_production_body: A precondition on the capture stub, not a claim about the harness. If it failed, the test could not have compared anything - it guards the comparison rather than making one.

Asserts about PRODUCTION, not the harness, so no mutation of the harness can redden it. It is a tripwire for the opposite direction: if production ever grows a cap, PLAN-0122 L-4 must be re-measured before this comparison means anything again.
exemptions.test_harness_timeout_follows_the_product: Green by construction under P2b as re-aimed (the probe copies the shipped value, so this conjunct holds). Reddening it needs a mutation returning something other than the shipped number, which is the same defect P2b already witnesses from the other side.

Co-falsified with : any mutation that stops the harness tracking the constant collapses both, and the driver credits only the assertion that fails first. Present as the anti-vacuity guard - without it, a resolver returning 3.0 unconditionally would satisfy the other two.
The explicit-flag path. No probe in this battery touches it because AC-2 is about the DEFAULT following production; a flag that stops working is a separate defect with no bearing on parity.
exemptions.test_both_transports_time_out_in_the_sam: The production side of the pair. No mutation of the harness can redden it, and mutating production is out of scope for a harness battery.
Production timing - same reason as above. It is the reference the harness figure is compared against.

Co-falsified with the harness raises-guard (#1), which P2c witnesses: if the call does not raise, the timing line is never reached. Measured, not assumed - P2c was first declared against THIS claim and the driver reported a MISFIRE naming the earlier line.
